items.title: From Deepfakes to Helpdesk Impersonation: Why Stronger Verification Matters
items.summary: Attackers use deepfakes, helpdesk impersonation, and fake IT support requests to deceive employees and gain unauthorized access. Specops Software examines real attacks and recommends stronger identity verification to counter social engineering.

items.title: British hacker gets 6 year sentence for $11.6M crypto theft scheme
items.summary: Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a six‑year sentence for leading a hacking collective that stole $11.6 million in cryptocurrency. Microsoft described the group as one of the most dangerous financial criminal groups.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Achieving the impossible: XSS in innerHTML without equals
items.summary: Researcher Masato Kinugawa discusses a novel XSS vulnerability that exploits innerHTML without equality checks, revealing new web security risks.

items.title: Open by Default, Already Occupied: Threat Actors are Renting your Compute
items.summary: Threat actors are renting cloud compute resources, taking advantage of default open configurations to host malicious workloads.

items.title: New EggStreme Malware Variant Goes Silent to Evade Security Tools in Government Attacks
items.summary: A Chinese APT group rebuilt the EggStreme malware to evade detection, targeting Philippine government organizations with silent variants that avoid security tools.

items.title: Major Brazilian Signature Apps Enable RCE & Fraud
items.summary: Brazilian government‑sanctioned authentication middleware contains remote code execution bugs, enabling fraud in critical legal documents.

items.title: Suspected Chinese APT Rebuilds EggStreme Malware After Exposure
items.summary: After exposure, a suspected Chinese APT reassembled EggStreme malware and its infrastructure to continue operations.

items.title: Ice hockey governing body website defaced amid dispute over Russia's exclusion
items.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation website was defaced with a pro‑Russian message amid disputes over Russia’s exclusion from competitions.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Russian APT Poses as Employee of Hacked Firm to Breach Another US Organization
items.summary: A Russian APT used stolen identities from a hacked firm to phish a U.S. organization, demonstrating advanced social engineering tactics.

items.title: Cyberattack hits Norwegian energy giant Equinor, disrupting internal services
items.summary: Equinor is addressing a cyberattack on its IT systems that disrupted internal services, but the company reports no impact on oil and gas production.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Last of Five Defendants Sentenced in US Scattered Spider Hacking Case
items.summary: British national Tyler Robert Buchanan sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison for his role in the Scattered Spider hacking case. The Department of Justice announced the sentence. This is the final defendant to be sentenced in the case.

items.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Allows Remote Attacks on Major Java Apps
items.summary: A critical OpenJDK flaw, known as Java4Shell, enables remote code execution on major Java applications. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency has urged organizations to apply mitigations. The vulnerability affects widely used Java apps.

items.title: New Attack Bypasses TPM Lockout to Crack Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs in Days, Not Years
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated that opening the PC case can reset the TPM lockout for Windows Hello and BitLocker PINs on AMD and some Intel systems. This allows attackers to guess short PINs within days. The study tested a four-digit Hello PIN and a six-digit BitLocker PIN.

items.title: Microsoft Takes Perception Agentic Security Platform Out of Preview
items.summary: Microsoft has moved its Perception Agentic Security Platform out of preview. Four blue team agents and the Recon Agent are now generally available. Integrations and vulnerability shielding remain in preview.

items.title: France Is Blaming Iran for the Fridge Cyberattack
items.summary: France attributes a recent fridge cyberattack to Iran, citing U.S. intelligence assessments. The assessment is low confidence, indicating fragmented evidence. The attribution remains unconfirmed.

items.title: CISO Conversations: Patti Degnan – Part of the Job Is Deciding What Not to Do
items.summary: Patti Degnan, whose identity was stolen in 2006, eventually became CISO at endpoint security firm Glow. The incident shaped her career path. She discusses decision-making in security roles.

items.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
items.summary: The Java4Shell vulnerability (CVE-2026-114938) permits unauthenticated remote code execution on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, and other applications. It exists in Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI support. The flaw was disclosed by Calif.

items.title: Dizigom illegal streaming service with 21M monthly visits shuts down
items.summary: The Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment announced the shutdown of Dizigom, a Turkish piracy site with 21 million monthly visits. The closure followed a settlement agreement with the operators. The site was one of Turkey's largest illegal streaming services.

items.title: Russian Espionage Actor Star Blizzard Focuses on Cloud Identities for Mass Data Theft
items.summary: Google analysis indicates that the Russian espionage group Star Blizzard, also known as Cold Relic, is increasingly targeting cloud identities. The group aims to steal data and facilitate further attacks. The focus represents a shift toward cloud-based threats.

items.title: Chrome 158 Patches 204 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Google released Chrome 158, which addresses 204 vulnerabilities. The company awarded $11,000 for five externally reported bugs and is determining payouts for 36 additional issues. The update improves browser security.

items.title: Java4Shell OpenJDK flaw: Exploitation is tricky and hinges on specific CPUs (CVE-2026-114938)
items.summary: Oracle and OpenJDK fixed CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption flaw in the Base64 decoder that could allow unauthenticated code execution on Java servers. No successful attacks have been reported.

items.title: Microsoft Agent Framework Releases Poisoned With Credential Stealer
items.summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of the agent-framework package on PyPI contain a credential stealer that captures Azure, Azure DevOps, and GitHub Actions credentials when Python starts.

items.title: The challenge of defending against bulletproof dead drops on public blockchains
items.summary: Malware command-and-control infrastructure is shifting from centralized servers to decentralized blockchain networks, creating resilient dead drops that eliminate single points of failure.

items.title: UAT-12643: Suspected North Korea-aligned actor blends blockchain resilience with targeted infostealing
items.summary: Cisco Talos identified malicious infrastructure linked to a financially motivated threat group, designated UAT-12643, that uses blockchain resilience for targeted information theft.

items.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks
items.summary: CVE-2026-115731 allows a client with any CA‑signed agent certificate to execute code on a Perforce Puppet server, and the flaw has been actively exploited in attacks.

items.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
items.summary: Apache released security updates for a critical Roller flaw that threat actors are exploiting to gain code execution on vulnerable servers.

items.title: Watchdog Warns UK Government Is Falling Short on Risk Management
items.summary: A National Audit Office report indicates that the UK government’s risk management practices are inadequate, leading to poor decision making.

items.title: Microsoft announces Windows Server 2028 with hardened security
items.summary: Microsoft unveiled Windows Server 2028 at Ignite 2026, highlighting enhanced security features for the next major server OS release.

items.title: Oracle Patches 950 Vulnerabilities With November 2026 CSPU
items.summary: Oracle’s November 2026 CSPU includes over 300 patches for unauthenticated remote exploits and 62 critical‑severity fixes, addressing 950 vulnerabilities.

items.title: Hackers Exploiting Critical Puppet RCE Flaw Affecting Enterprise Management Servers
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-115731 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after reports of active exploitation of a critical Perforce Puppet RCE affecting enterprise management servers.

items.title: CISA Urges Immediate Patching of Java4Shell Flaw That Could Allow Remote Code Execution
items.summary: CISA urges immediate patching of Oracle Java CVE-2026-114938, a critical out‑of‑bounds write that can lead to denial‑of‑service or remote code execution.

items.title: British Scattered Spider hacker sentenced to 6 years in prison
items.summary: A leader of the Scattered Spider cybercrime collective was sentenced to six years in U.S. prison for cryptocurrency theft and conspiracy to hack multiple companies.

items.title: Java4Shell Vulnerability Puts Many Enterprise Applications at Risk of Takeover
items.summary: Java4Shell allows remote code execution in applications such as Jira, Jenkins, and Keycloak; real‑world exploitation requires target‑specific work.

items.title: Deutsche Telekom IoT’s CEO on securing devices that run for 20 years
items.summary: Deutsche Telekom IoT CEO Christian Schwalbe discusses risks of devices that remain in service for 15–20 years and how the EU Cyber Resilience Act and traffic‑pattern analysis can help secure them.

items.title: Once a scam ends the victim blaming begins
items.summary: Cyberpsychologist Dr. Nicola Fox Hamilton highlights how blaming scam victims deepens harm and discourages future reporting, emphasizing the psychological impact of phishing.

items.title: The forced audit: how AuditTeam’s OpsAgent framework masks ransomware as consulting
items.summary: AuditTeam’s OpsAgent ransomware uses a forced audit model, demanding consulting fees to delete stolen data, and is distributed via a Rust rewrite of the implant.

items.title: Attackers Compromise Microsoft's Agent Framework PyPI Package to Steal Cloud Credentials
items.summary: Threat actors released malicious versions of Microsoft’s agent‑framework PyPI package (1.26.1 and 1.26.2) that install a credential stealer on every Python startup, targeting cloud credentials.

items.title: TapMap: Free, open-source network map
items.summary: TapMap is a free desktop application that visualizes a computer’s active network connections on an interactive world map using local GeoIP data.

items.title: BubbleLoader malware turns copies of WinRAR and Windows Media Player into carriers
items.summary: BubbleLoader modifies the entry point of legitimate Windows programs, such as WinRAR and Windows Media Player, embedding hidden code and PNG images to act as carriers for additional malware.

items.title: Russian COLD RELIC Hackers Use Stolen Google Workspace Data to Breach Second U.S. Organization
items.summary: Cold Relic leveraged stolen Google Workspace data to compromise a second U.S. organization, using a single cloud breach as a launchpad for linked intrusions.

items.title: Uber says nearly 150,000 impacted by third-party breach
items.summary:
Uber notified that a third‑party service provider stole internal credentials and accessed Uber’s account, affecting about 150,000 users.
The breach was discovered on October 9.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Critical Java4Shell flaw allows RCE attacks on major Java applications
items.summary: Java4Shell vulnerability in OpenJDK allows unauthenticated remote code execution on popular enterprise Java applications such as Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak.

items.title: Optimizely Malware Attacks Highlight Third-Party Vendor Risks
items.summary: At least 178 organizations were exposed to hydra‑like malware through a third‑party platform, highlighting risks from external vendors.

items.title: Cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds
items.summary: Credentials and secrets published in public Docker Hub images are being extracted and exploited within as little as eight seconds of release.

items.title: Website management platform Optimizely confirms hackers put malicious code into customer sites
items.summary: Optimizely confirmed that malicious JavaScript was injected into 178 customer websites via its Web experimentation platform.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: GSA says post-quantum work on PIV cards shows new encryption can work on old tech
items.summary: The GSA reports that post‑quantum encryption can be implemented on legacy PIV smart cards, addressing compatibility and visibility gaps.

items.title: How CISA is prioritizing companies for talks about security improvements
items.summary: CISA is prioritizing outreach to companies to discuss security improvements, as highlighted in a recent FedTalks presentation.

items.title: Japan takes Fugaku supercomputer offlline after cyberattack
items.summary: Japan's RIKEN Center has taken the Fugaku supercomputer offline following a security breach.

items.title: Borrowed Code, Real Consequences: What OPTIMJACK Teaches Us
items.summary: The OPTIMJACK supply‑chain attack shows how a compromised vendor script can expose websites, emphasizing the need for strict segmentation.

items.title: Researchers Claim Two RCE Exploits That Bypass Telegram’s New Android Defenses
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated two remote code execution exploits that bypass Telegram's recent Android security filter via malicious widgets.

items.title: Apple reports outages affecting iCloud Mail, AppleCare and more
items.summary: Apple reported service disruptions affecting iCloud Mail, iCloud Account & Sign In, Apple School Manager, and Schoolwork.

items.title: Kazakh ransomware hacking suspect extradited from Italy
items.summary: Roman Khlynovskiy, accused of ransomware attacks on healthcare, schools, and businesses, was extradited from Italy to the U.S. He is linked to the "8 Digits Team" and associated with INC and Lynx.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: CVE-2026-114938: Reported Critical Pre-authentication Remote Code Execution in Java 17
items.summary: CVE-2026-114938 is a memory corruption vulnerability in Java 17+ that could allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability has a preliminary CVSSv4 score of 9.2 and is under investigation by Oracle and OpenJDK.

items.title: Tor releases emergency update amid ongoing DDoS attack
items.summary: The Tor Project issued a security update for its relay software to mitigate an ongoing distributed denial‑of‑service attack. The update aims to protect relays and operators from the attack’s impact.

items.title: California fines Hertz $1.5 million for breaking state data privacy law
items.summary: Hertz agreed to a $1.5 million fine imposed by the California Privacy Protection Agency for violating state data privacy regulations. The company will adjust its business practices to comply with the law.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: NSA Net, agency’s classified internal network, faces unspecified disruptions
items.summary: The NSA’s classified internal network, NSA Net, experienced disruptions, prompting staggered arrivals at Fort Meade headquarters. Technicians are working to restore full network functionality.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Flipper Devices launches $399 ‘Flipper One’ Linux-based multi-tool
items.summary: Flipper Devices launched a crowdfunding campaign for the Flipper One, a $399 portable Linux computer and networking multi‑tool. The device builds on the company’s popular Flipper Zero pentesting hardware.

items.title: Windows 11 previews remote padlock only IT can open
items.summary: Windows 11 preview introduces an Intune feature that blocks normal sign‑ins unless IT unlocks the device, preserving data. A separate test build removes Offline Maps settings.

items.title: Oracle to Patch 11 Java Flaws Today as Critical OpenJDK RCE (CVE-2026-114938) Report Emerges
items.summary: Oracle will release patches for 11 Java SE vulnerabilities that may allow unauthenticated remote code execution. The flaws carry a maximum CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1 and include the critical CVE-2026-114938.

items.title: Inside Modern Phishing Kits Built to Steal Microsoft 365 Sessions
items.summary: Huntress researchers dissect EvilTokens, Knight Office, and Kali365 phishing kits that capture and replay Microsoft 365 session tokens, and outline detection and containment steps.

items.title: Market Research Giant Ipsos Investigating Breach of Internal System
items.summary: Ipsos publicly disclosed a breach of its internal system on Nov. 16, five days after filing a complaint with authorities, and is investigating the incident.

items.title: Envoy Visitors Critical turns visitor policies into approval workflows
items.summary: Envoy launched Visitors Critical, a visitor security solution that combines identity verification, screening, and approval workflows on a shared architecture for high‑consequence environments.

items.title: Fandango Warns Ticket Buyers of Payment Card Data Exposure
items.summary: Fandango warned customers that card numbers, CVVs, expiration dates, and email addresses used during checkout over four days in October may have been exposed.

items.title: Autistic teen hacker pleads guilty to leak of Grand Theft Auto VI footage
items.summary: 21‑year‑old Artion Kurtaj pleaded guilty to leaking Grand Theft Auto VI footage in 2022 before the game's release.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: AppGate Optimizer helps teams narrow access without disrupting users
items.summary: AppGate released AppGate Optimizer GA to help organizations reduce over‑provisioned access, streamline reviews, and demonstrate least privilege to auditors by analyzing user access and recommending precise changes.

items.title: Pakistani hackers are spying on defense workers with fake job sites
items.summary: Pakistani hackers used fake job sites to target Indian job seekers, potentially aiming at defense contractors and military personnel.

items.title: Optimizely Flaw Exploited to Serve Malicious Code to Visitors of 178 Organizations
items.summary: An attacker exploited an Optimizely vulnerability to inject malicious code into the websites of 178 organizations, delivering malware to visitors.

items.title: Suspected ransomware affiliate extradited to US over $500 million in extortion demands
items.summary: A 43‑year‑old Kazakh national, alleged to be part of the 8‑Digits Team linked to INC and Lynx ransomware, was extradited from Italy to the US for involvement in data theft from hospitals and schools and extortion demands totaling $500 million.

items.title: 'Not rocket surgery' claims researcher who found six Danfoss fridge controller zero-days in under an hour
items.summary:
Researchers identified six zero‑day vulnerabilities in Danfoss refrigerator controllers, including a flaw in strict authentication and missing basic exploit defenses.
The exploits were discovered in under an hour.

items.title: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
items.summary: A month‑long campaign targeted MSP ScreenConnect servers, sending over 688,000 exploit requests for CVE‑2026‑84869 to run guest‑pushed files on more than 40 servers.

items.title: Alleged ransomware group member extradited from Italy to face US charges in hospital, school extortion case
items.summary: A Kazakh national was extradited from Italy to the United States to face charges for a ransomware and extortion plot against hospitals and schools, including violations of the TAKE IT DOWN Act.

items.title: Microsoft Warns of Coordinated Phishing Campaign Leveraging M365 Service Outage
items.summary: Microsoft warned of a coordinated phishing campaign exploiting a Microsoft 365 service outage to harvest credentials, urging organizations to check for compromise.

items.title: Access Dental Management Data Breach Impacts Over 340,000
items.summary: Access Dental Management suffered a data breach that exposed personal, health, and insurance data of more than 340,000 patients after a network intrusion.

items.title: Corma Receives $125 Million to Train Foundation Models for Defensive Cybersecurity
items.summary: Corma raised $125 million in funding, led by NEA, to develop foundation models for defensive cybersecurity, valuing the company at $1 billion.

items.title: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
items.summary: N‑able released patches for 17 N‑central zero‑days and removed legacy APIs, addressing both newly disclosed and already exploited vulnerabilities.

items.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
items.summary:
Hackers bypassed GitHub SHA pinning by injecting malicious code into the Trivy security scanner, demonstrating a gap in supply‑chain defenses.
A webinar explains remediation steps.

items.title: Researchers Detail iPhone Flaw That Let Apps Record Audio Despite Denied Microphone Permission
items.summary:
Apple patched an audio service flaw that allowed apps to record audio on iOS devices even after microphone permission was denied.
The vulnerability was disclosed by Meta researchers and fixed in August.

items.title: Opinion pollster Ipsos 'fesses up to 'cybersecurity incident'
items.summary: Ipsos admitted a cybersecurity incident and hired external specialists to investigate its cause and scope.

items.title: New GitDoor and GraphDoor Backdoors Turn GitHub and SharePoint Into Covert C2 Channels
items.summary:
Operation ShadowCloud, identified by Kaspersky, targets government sectors in Asia and Africa.
The campaign installs GitDoor and GraphDoor backdoors that use GitHub and SharePoint as covert command‑and‑control channels.

items.title: Microsoft testing Remote Lock for lost or stolen Windows devices
items.summary: Microsoft is testing a Remote Lock feature that allows enterprise IT administrators to lock lost or stolen Windows devices without wiping them.

items.title: The Super Intelligence Task Force should open the door to defenders
items.summary:
AI models are finding software vulnerabilities faster than organizations can remediate them.
HackerOne data shows a 131% increase in valid report backlog and rising critical findings, while remediation lags.

items.title: Optimizely Vulnerability Exploited to Serve Malware on Major Websites
items.summary: An Optimizely vulnerability was exploited to deliver malware to major websites, including BBC, CNN, Zoom, GitLab, Salesforce, Equifax, HSBC, and IKEA.

items.title: ICO Issues GTA 6 Scam Warning as Release Date Nears
items.summary: The UK Information Commissioner’s Office has issued a warning about Grand Theft Auto 6‑related cyber‑attacks as the game’s release date approaches.

items.title: Court clears brothers of $25 million Ethereum crypto heist charges
items.summary: A US District Judge acquitted two brothers of a $25 million Ethereum crypto‑heist, which involved exploiting a bug in the Ethereum blockchain.

items.title: Fully Autonomous Agentic Attacks Are Three Months Away, Google Warns
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group warns that fully autonomous agentic attacks could emerge in three months, signaling a shift in penetration‑testing frameworks.

items.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 2
items.summary: Part 2 of the Operation ShadowCloud analysis details the GraphDoor backdoor, additional plug‑ins, and technical attribution of the campaign.

items.title: Operation ShadowCloud: cloud service–based backdoors targeting government networks in Asia and Africa. Part 1
items.summary: Part 1 of the Operation ShadowCloud analysis covers the initial infection stage, the GitDoor backdoor using GitHub as C2, and the shellcode families it loads.

items.title: Ransomware affiliate suspect extradited to US, faces 27 years in prison
items.summary: A Kazakh national extradited from Italy faces 27 years in prison in the US for ransomware attacks targeting schools, hospitals, and healthcare entities.

items.title: ConnectWise Warns ScreenConnect Attacks Continue as SCKit Targets Unpatched Systems
items.summary: ConnectWise investigated unauthorized access to ScreenConnect partner environments. Customers are advised to use technician client version 26.6.5 or newer. On‑premises activity continues when third‑party extensions remain enabled.

items.title: Japan's Fugaku supercomputer has decidedly un-super security
items.summary: Attackers attempted to log into Japan’s Fugaku supercomputer after credentials were exposed on its status page.

items.title: N-able Patches 17 N-central Flaws as Attackers Exploit Earlier Bugs to Deploy Crypto Miners
items.summary: N‑able released a security update that patches 17 critical N‑central flaws, enhancing the Remote Monitoring and Management and Unified Endpoint Management platform.

items.title: Optimizely hack infected CNN, Fox News, BBC, Salesforce sites with malware
items.summary: A supply‑chain attack on Optimizely injected malicious JavaScript into sites such as CNN, Fox News, BBC, and Salesforce, targeting cryptocurrency and payment data and exploiting iOS vulnerabilities.

items.title: QUIC and Covert: Novel HTTP/3-Powered RATs Target Southeast Asian Governments
items.summary:
Unit 42 uncovered a cyberespionage campaign targeting Southeast Asian governments.
The attackers used PerfectPioneer RAT, modular KUKURAT, and stealth HTTP/3 C2 channels.

items.title: Google Project Zero Slashes Bug Disclosure Deadlines, Splitting Experts
items.summary:
Google Project Zero announced it will shorten public disclosure timelines for vendors from 120 days to 30 days.
The change will roll out over the next 14 months.

items.title: Infoblox customer and staff data exposed in Sharepoint breach
items.summary:
Infoblox is investigating a SharePoint breach that exposed customer and staff data.
Details of the breach remain limited.

items.title: California sues OpenAI for Hugging Face and other incidents, alleging deception and recklessness
items.summary:
California filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging deception and recklessness.
The state claims OpenAI withheld incident details from the Attorney General.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Match fined $10 million for alleged Tinder privacy violations
items.summary:
Ireland’s data protection regulator fined Match Group $10 million for Tinder’s failure to provide users with their personal data upon request.
The fine addresses privacy violations.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: ‘123456’ has been the world’s most popular password for 7 out of the last 8 years
items.summary:
The password "123456" remains the most commonly used worldwide, dominating for 7 of the past 8 years.
Security experts warn against using simple passwords.

items.title: NoisyTCP bug gives Linux servers a remote crash problem 11 years in the making
items.summary:
A long‑standing NoisyTCP flaw can cause remote crashes on Linux servers.
The vulnerability affects services even when running inside a container.

items.title: Rapid7 Detected Exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center, N-able N-central also Exploited
items.summary:
Rapid7 identified exploitation of CVE-2026-90436, a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability in Apache Axis.
The flaw affected Atlassian Confluence and N‑able N‑central.

items.title: Italian regulator fines Meta $886 million for violating data privacy law
items.summary:
Italy’s data regulator fined Meta $886 million for alleged misuse of Android users’ photo galleries to recommend content.
The fine cites violations of privacy laws.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: King Charles opens new HQ for National Cyber Force, UK’s offensive hacking unit
items.summary: UK's National Cyber Force opens a new headquarters in Samlesbury, Lancashire, housing the country's offensive cyber operations team.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Crook turns free trials into phishing factory, as LearnWorlds sends 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices
items.summary: LearnWorlds sent 13,000 fake YouTube copyright notices to free‑trial users, created 570 bogus accounts and a fake YouTube page, but the CEO denies a breach.

items.title: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
items.summary: Microsoft attributes last week's global Microsoft 365 outage to a software bug introduced in July, which caused cascading failures that left over 80% of gateway servers unresponsive.

items.title: From view-only access to container root: five vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs (FIXED)
items.summary: Rapid7 identified five vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs that allow an attacker with view‑only access to chain exploits and execute arbitrary OS commands as root within the DocumentServer container, also exposing hidden server files and document data.

items.title: Typosquatters Target New Brand Domains Within 24 Hours of Registration
items.summary: Symantec reports attackers target newly registered domains that mimic well‑known brands within 24 hours, using lookalike sites to facilitate malicious follow‑on activity.

items.title: Fandango says hackers stole payment card details from checkout pages
items.summary: Fandango Media confirms a data breach that exposed payment card details entered on its checkout pages and advises customers to monitor accounts.

items.title: Google Project Zero Sets Course for 30-Day Disclosure Deadline
items.summary: Google Project Zero will adopt a 30‑day vulnerability disclosure window starting January 2028, moving from a 60‑day window in February 2027 to accelerate responsible disclosure.

items.title: La Poste Subsidiary Maileva Breach Exposes 22 Million People
items.summary: Maileva, a La Poste subsidiary, suffered a breach that exposed names and postal addresses of 22 million individuals.

items.title: NIST Finalizes Post-Quantum Cryptography Guidance, GAO Offers a Reality Check
items.summary: NIST finalized guidance on post‑quantum cryptography, while a GAO report notes that many agencies are behind in building defenses against the technology.

items.title: Is it safe to upload my passport or ID online?
items.summary: The article explains how to reduce risk when uploading passports or ID documents online to third‑party services.
